Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to begin my evaluation, how soon after birth did these symptoms start, and were you born prematurely?

REQUEST TEST: Apgar_Scores
REQUEST TEST: Maternal_History

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Apgar_Scores: Not provided; Maternal_History: Not provided. NORMAL READINGS (regarding requested specific test values as they are not in the provided data).

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of grunting and intercostal retractions suggest significant respiratory effort; however, I cannot accept the suggestion of Tuberculosis without further evidence given the patient's age. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray to visualize the lung fields immediately.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray findings of fine reticular granulation with a ground-glass appearance are classic for respiratory distress syndrome in a newborn; to confirm this, I need to know your gestational age and whether you were born before 34 weeks. REQUEST TEST: Gestational_Age

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical presentation of grunting, retractions, and peripheral cyanosis, combined with a gestational age of 33 weeks and characteristic ground-glass opacity on chest X-ray, confirms this diagnosis.
